title: The Alcove Behind the Tapestry
description: You press past the edge of a heavy tapestry — its woven figures worn to near-nothing by years and damp — and find a shallow alcove behind it, barely wide enough for a person. A stone bench runs along the back wall, and the air here is still in a way the rest of the manor is not. No sound reaches you. The tapestry falls back into place, and the hall beyond disappears.

choices.label: Sit and rest a while
choices.description: Settle onto the bench and let the stillness do its work.

success.narrative: You sit in the dark until your breathing slows and the ache behind your eyes loosens, just enough.

choices.label: Rest briefly, then press on
choices.description: A moment off your feet, no more — you do not trust the quiet.

success.narrative: The brief pause is enough to ease the tightness in your legs, even if the stillness here unsettles you as much as it helps.

choices.label: Leave immediately
choices.description: Something about a hiding place inside the manor does not sit right.

success.narrative: You step back through the tapestry into the hall, no worse than before.

visual.alt_text: A narrow stone alcove hidden behind a faded tapestry, a low bench against the back wall, the space barely lit and entirely still.
